To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C+ G content is highly correlated with the chromosome length in Proteobacteria and Ascomycota, but is not correlated with chromosome length in Archaea, and is likely to be positively correlated with chromosome length also in some plants.
C+G content varies greatly in microorganisms, is similar within each animal/plant subkingdom, and is correlated with genome/chromosomal size in bacteria but not in other phyla.
the C+Gs content in the genome and in the chromosomes is under the genetic control by both the cis- and trans- factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution, variation, and correlation analysis of C+G content with genome/chromosome sizes in different kingdoms/phyla.
the variation, evolution, and correlation analysis of genome size and base composition in different kingdoms and phyla.
the correlation between genome size and chromosome size in different kingdoms, and the correlation between C + G content and chromosome size.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no simple correlation between C+ G content and chromosome size.
the relationship between C+G and chromosome length varies among kingdoms, groups, and species.
C+G content in chromosomes is under genetic control and that it is positively correlated with chromosome length in some phyla, such as Proteobacteria and Ascomycota, but not in others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C+C content and the genome/chromosome size are under genetic control and are correlated in some phyla but not others.
the correlation between chromosome size and C+G-content varies among different phyla and species.
the C+ G content is under both cis- and trans- factors and that correlation can be positive, or negative, or insignificant in different phyla.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between C+G and genome/chromosome size is very complex and that the relationship is not universal.
the C+C content and chromosome length are not correlated across all kingdoms and phyla.
the C+C content is not a good predictor of the chromosome size and vice versa, and that these parameters are under independent control.
